title: ROME rank-one updates encoded by factual Mirror coordinates
hypothesis: For facts whose ROME keys and output deltas lie on fixed two-dimensional rotation orbits, shared key/value bases plus two angles per fact will preserve rank-one edit efficacy and specificity while using fewer actual serialized bytes than storing each ROME key/value factor; arbitrary off-orbit facts will require private residual state.
physical_object: one shared key plane and one shared output-delta plane
mirror_coordinate: per-fact key angle and output angle generating the ROME rank-one factors
logical_multiplicity: 64 standalone factual rank-one edits addressed by distinct View coordinates
controls: ROME per-fact full-precision key and value factors
generic shared two-plane basis with per-fact coefficients
Mirror angle codes with explicitly charged off-orbit residual

task.aligned: key and value each have fixed norm and rotate in preregistered 2D planes
task.specificity: edited-key target error and random/orthogonal query drift

development.allowed: choose rotation-plane construction and numerical tolerances only; no fresh access

success_gate: Every fresh world: Mirror aligned edit error <=1e-5, specificity drift <=1e-5, and N64 actual payload <=80% of full ROME factors; generic basis is compared for Mirror-specific value.
failure_gate: Mirror misses any efficacy/specificity/byte gate, or generic coefficient control is equal/fewer bytes at equal quality.
boundaries: Analytic linear ROME mechanism screen, not a Transformer or factual language evaluation.
Mirror coordinates use the known aligned orbit; no claim of discovering factual structure.
Each edit is evaluated as a selected standalone update; cumulative multi-edit interference is deferred to MA-472.
